I am.', 'Big fucking surprise...', 'They hire psycho scum, arm them to the teeth and let them loose in the city. What do you think is gonna happen?', 'What do you mean *okay*?', 'He jerks forward a bit.', "No, they won't.", 'Get out of here with your negative energy.', "No wonder you cops get shot to shit every day -- can't go to war with an attitude like *that*.", 'Goddamn right we do.', "We've done it before. Ain't that right, fellas?!", 'Yeah...', 'Just try not to get in the way -- when the whoop-ass flies open!', "We don't need you or your lost gun. We all *have* our guns.", "We'll just use those if it's okay with you.", 'Okay, I accept the offer.', "But I'll believe it when I see it.", "Funny. Don't get hit by a stray bullet.", "Goddamn right it's nothing. The fuck are they gonna do? We got ten thousand men in the Union."]

Title: Disco Elysium
Dialogues: ["Out of old habit he still snaps his fingers at you -- but then stops immediately, realizing what he's done. He does not want to talk to you.", "Stuck in the rain in a traffic jam, man. What's on your mind?", 'Okay...', 'He seems a little apprehensive.', 'What?', 'Sorry?', "Is she *dead*? Don't tell me she's...", "Look, man, fuck off, okay? Fuck off and let me have a panic attack. I don't need to know about this shit anymore. I can't talk to cops any more...", 'I *told* you not to go after her! I TOLD you.', 'What happened? Is she... is she...', "Don't tell me. Just back off and don't talk to me again, okay? I can't talk to cops anymore. I can't be involved in this shit.", 'Just *happened*?', "Is she *dead*? Don't tell me she's...", 'His eyes grow wide and he hyperventilates.', "Is she *dead*? Don't tell me she's...", 'God damn, this shit is too intense for me...', "I don't wanna know, man. I don't wanna know if she even got away...", "That breath of his isn't calming down.", 'Man, I need to take a breath here, excuse me...', 'Whooh... good on her. And good on *you* too -- better focus your efforts on the bad guys. Mercs and such. Plenty of baddies to go around...', "And she didn't do it, believe me. If it's something *bad* then she didn't do it. Didn't know her for long but I know people.", 'Whooh... good on her. And good on *you* too -- better focus your efforts on the bad guys. Mercs and such. Plenty of baddies to go around...', "And she didn't do it -- believe me. If it's something *bad* then she didn't do it. Didn't know her for long but I know people.", "Whooh... good on her. And good on *you* too, my man. That's...", 'He looks for the words...', '*Merciful*. Downright merciful -- you cops keep exercising *that* muscle and people will be more willing to cooperate, you know.', "That's probably for the best. You keep your job to yourself -- with a job like yours, you *have* to.", "I don't want to talk about that...", 'He shifts around, suddenly uncomfortable, then looks away.', "Man, I was hoping it isn't gonna be her...", "All I can say is -- she isn't around here anymore; she isn't some evil drug-trafficker; and I don't know where she is.", "I didn't, man -- I told you, I was *hoping* it's not her. That she wouldn't be mixed up in it.", "Thank god I *don't know*. People here call her 'the lady driver.' She kept her name a secret. From me, too. Now I see why.", "A friend? An acquaintance. I don't know... She was the only person in this damn jam I could talk to. She's someone I don't want to rat out to the law, okay?", 'A young-ish woman. Gruff, but... in a cool way.', 'Blue and violet, dyed.', 'It was violet when she got here. Blue before she went.', "Damn, I don't wanna...", "Please just let it go. Whatever she did, it can't be that bad. She's not a bad person, I know that much.", "That's how it always is with you, isn't it? All part of the investigation...", "The girl's *troubled* -- if you hunt her down, she may not survive it. I can't have that on my conscience.", "I don't believe you.", "I just can't, man. I'm not *naive*.", "She's got the *darkness* in her. That young person's darkness when you think it's all over. And you're looking for a way *out*.", "Yes, which is why I don't want to *snitch* on her.", "It's snitching, man. I know what it is.", "I heard the rumours. I saw the others drivers looking at me *strange* when we talked. And she told me too -- that she's had a violent life. But I wasn't afraid of her, more like *for* her.", 'Well...', "It looks like it did *now* -- but we didn't talk about that. We talked about life, you know. She talked about her mind...", 'The way it worked. The trouble it was giving her.', "Fuck, man... Go grill someone else with these questions, okay? There are plenty of drivers here who couldn't stand her. Or were *afraid* of her. They'd be more than happy to rat her out.", "Fine. I don't want to be a butcher. And I don't want to be a knight either. I just wanna be a person who can sleep at night. A little fame wouldn't hurt too.", "You're not gonna put a bullet in your head if you blow it, are you? 'Cause she's on the *edge*, man.", 'I... I thought you were a different kind of cop.', 'Something breaks in him as he stares into your eyes.', 'Here.', 'He takes a keyring from his pocket -- then looks at it before giving it to you. In silence...', "The cabin is green. You can get in there with these. That's all I know.", 'Last Friday.', 'He blinks, his eyes half-empty now.', 'Last Friday.', 'He blinks, his eyes half-empty now.', "No. I don't know.", 'She left them to me. Because she trusted me... So I can get it out of the way when the jam breaks loose. Otherwise...', "He doesn't finish the sentence.", 'I bet you are.', 'Nah. I need to think my own thoughts now. Pray forgiveness for my sins. Go check your cabin...', 'I hope it gets you something. Helps someone.', "You don't *really* think so.", 'Thank you, friend.', 'Wow, this makes me feel like I should pick up smoking again... Would help with my rhymes too.', 'Whooh. Almost gave me a heart attack...', 'Yeah, I *really* need to start smoking again.', "Maybe. But not *another* person's life.", "Man, I was hoping she'd catch a break.", "All I can say is: she isn't around here anymore. She isn't some mastermind evil-doer. And I don't know where she is.", 'The man taps his fingers rhythmically against his arm.', 'What?', "But I *told* you she's my friend! Please don't make me give her up, detective. Get someone else. There's a *ton* of drivers here...", "Nope. Don't smoke.", 'He nods toward the big lorry behind him...', "Some of the other drivers do, though. There's still a few around, waiting for the Jam to disperse. Or waiting for the sweet release of death.", 'Man, relax. I quit, been clean for some time. There are some commitments you have to honour.', 'He looks at you with compassion in his eyes.', "It's a bad habit. You ought to quit, too.", 'No, my man, you asked for my cigarettes.', "There's sadness in his voice; he doesn't seem offended, though.", 'Anything else I can help you with?', 'Okay, man, I believe you.', 'He gives you a funny look.', "It's never a good time to quit.", 'You just gotta sit it out, friend.', 'Right, man -- *anew*.', 'The phoenix at the traffic jam.', 'Okay...', "But this is my last one. And it's a bad habit. You should quit before both of us have lung cancer.", 'You could also check the kiosque down the street. Frittte.', 'With three t-s. Revachol is weird...', 'Huh?', "Oh. No, I ain't got any money. They don't want to pay for unfinished work.", 'The bosses, man.', 'Makes sense? It sucks is what it does.', "Yeah, it sure ain't good for me -- or you. I'd spare a coin or two for a city cop down on his luck. If I had, say, *four* myself.", 'Dunno. Whatcha need?', "It's like... whatever's going on over at the docks. Workers got a blockade set up. Making demands. No way in or out.", "Maybe you should. Cops don't get paid much and the hours are long. Plus, you can get shot. Why not?", 'Some pretty wild stuff, I hear. Like a giant new power-crane and half the company? I forget *what* exactly. Good on them, I guess...', "I've heard talk there's a company rep in town too. Like... a strike negotiator type. They'd know what's up. Precise demands and so on.", 'They want to keep that money flowing in, my man.', "He makes a 'ka-ching' sound.", 'Anything else?', "Yeah, this ain't really my area of expertise. I just do my job and get paid. I have things to do and places to be. All of us do.", 'Us lorry drivers. Camionneurs. A few still hang around here waiting for this mess to end. Most have scurried off somewhere. To get drunk, or high. Or laid.', "Not that I blame 'em, really.", "Not my thing. Chasin' transient pleasures is a drag these days. I prefer the examined life now -- thinkin', reflectin', observin'.", 'He glances down the road toward the horizon, a glint of... something in his eyes.', "He ain't one of us drivers -- I know that. All accounted for. Otherwise, I haven't really asked about that. Been wastin' time right here. Keepin' busy.", "Analysin' the fundamental structural and psychological conditions of being stranded in the midst of a sea of motor lorries and their sad, despondent chauffeurs.", 'Nothing.', "I'm just messing with you, man. Don't mind my idle verbosity.", "A sense of surprise there ain't more bodies hanging from more trees.", 'Oh, high-grade narcotics. Illegal fire-arms. Stuff like that.', "Hah, no. I'm joking, my man.", 'FALN runs a nice, clean business. This haul of cargo is mostly sporting goods. You know, tracksuits and that kinda thing.', "They usually get shipped to Graad and the Occident. Though we've been making headway in the Iilmaraan market lately.", "Not unless they've illegalized sports equipment while I was on the road.", "This rockin' beauty?", "Sure is, like a rash you can't get rid of. You interested in heavy duty cargo machinery?", "Good eye, my man. Yup, she's an old one, but reliable.", 'Me and her spent a *long* time together.', "Neat -- for carrying large quantities of cargo a long distance. These FALN tracksuits need to find their way to the kids way out in Uamrao and L'Iramburde somehow...", "Yeah, must be -- your job's to know all those *little* things isn't it? While my job...", 'is to deliver tracksuit trousers.', "We're pals and all, but I can't just freely hand out the merchandise. The bosses won't be happy.", "Can't even get a few jokes past you, my man.", "I've got another haul of FALN cargo. Mostly sporting goods. Tracksuits and that kinda thing.", 'Ah, man, me and narcotics go way back.', "Had some good times surfin' the psychic waves of my own consciousness, you know?", 'But...', 'Those days are behind me. There are other addictions in my life now. Why the inquiry, my man?', "Hey man, that's serious criminal talk. Are you trying to pull some sort of an... entrapment thing on me?", "Yes, it's like... trying to trick a person into doing something criminal that they'd never do.", 'Then what are you trying to accomplish?', "Not me, man, no way. I don't need any trouble. Shit's bad enough anyway. This jam's got folks up in arms and I'm afraid it's headed toward a conflagration.", "Gotta guard the stuff -- bosses don't look kindly on missing cargo. And it gives me time to work on my rhymes.", "Look, man, I try to stay away from the criminal underbelly of Revachol. I'm a guest here. You really need to find another man to probe with those questions.", "So, you do realize entrapment doesn't work if you announce you're going to do it in advance?", 'He rubs his jaw.', "Then what's your deal here?", "It's hard to say. His gaze wanders southwest -- down the street that goes beyond the horizon...", 'Excuse me?', 'He emerges from the reverie.', 'He chuckles.', "There are things even a cop can't fix, my man. There's no helping an absence, you know?", "I miss my family. They're all I have, my wife... a second kid on the way... waiting all the way in Deora. And here I am, stuck in this shit, so far from home.", "Deora-of-the-Seven-Seas. It's on the other end of Le Caillou, pretty much -- on another island, called Laurentide, off mainland. We've got a little place there. I can almost hear my kid laugh, when it snows...", "What's it *like*? Good. And bad. An ache that brings you joy.", 'I think of them a lot. I dream up these silly scenarios, in great detail. Of living with them... it comforts me.', "There's a pause and a sigh. Then he turns his eyes to you.", 'What about you, cop-man? You missing someone?', "You lost your gun? Oh man, that's bad news. Especially here, in Martinaise. I hope you find it soon before things turn foul.", "But... thanks for this. It's nice to talk to someone. And I know it wasn't easy to ask.", 'I hope you find your way through your own troubles.', "I feel for you, my friend. It's good to miss someone. I like it. Knowing there's something *more* than what I have with me here.", "I feel for you, my friend. It's bad enough to *know* who you miss... missing like that doesn't feel like it has much of an upside.", 'Hunted? By what?', 'An ex-wife?', "Sinister presence? Wow... that sounds really bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage.", "Man, who even knows? It's like a legal contract, but also a bond between spirits... Every one is different, that's all I can say.", "Maybe it is. We're doing our best to keep ours together. I *hope* it's not, but you never know...", "Thanks for the dark words, I guess. I'll make sure they don't come true.", "It's good talking to someone. I know it wasn't easy to say those things, so...", 'I hope you find your way through your own troubles.', "Yeah... In marriage you never know if you're doing the right thing. I *hope* we're doing our best to keep ours together, but -- anything can happen. Look, man...", "Thanks for this. It's nice to talk to someone. I know it wasn't easy to ask, so....", 'I hope you find your way through your own troubles.', 'Sure, man, if you say so...', 'But look, man...', "Thanks for this. It's good to talk to someone. I know it wasn't easy to ask, so....", 'I hope you find your way through your own troubles.', "Planar hunter? Wow... that sounds really bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage.", "Black reverb? Wow... that sounds really bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage.", "A great white ghost? Wow... that sounds really bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage.", "Still -- a shadowy figure. That sounds pretty bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage...", "Sure man, no problem... and thanks for this. It's good to talk to someone. I know it wasn't easy to ask.", 'I hope you find your way through your own troubles.', 'Man.', "I don't know what to say. Not much anyone can do... there's no helping an absence, you know?", "I'm okay, man. Just... the jam's got me down. The fumes, the chemical rainbows, the tarpaulin stretched on the frames and the dull engines off...", 'The man recedes into his daze of words.', "Man, nothing's troubling me. Just the usual lorryman tropes and hopes: the road and the rhymes. This jam ain't helping either...", 'He looks around.', "Cool, cool... We all want to know each other, know each other's woes and all -- but people, man, they have *slippery* souls...", 'Whoa.', 'What else?', "Silent communion, that's good...", "He's transfixed by the words.", "That's some *great* shit. You came up with that yourself?", "No matter. Great verse is like that sometimes -- ephemeral. You might not look it, but seems you have some literary chops. Maybe there's hope for me yet!", "Just messin' with you. It's cool, you're an okay guy, for a cop.", "They're more often into fists than rhymes, see. Let alone *honesty in verse*.", "Well. You've given *me* some hope, I guess!", 'He gives you a thumbs up.', 'Umm... if you say so, officer.', 'He gives you a cautious thumbs up.', "No matter, it's a fine stanza. You're not so bad after all, for a cop.", "Right. But really -- no bullshit. That's great stuff. I sorta wanna know if it's yours...", "Fuckin' A! Seems I got you all wrong. Cops aren't much known for their artistic sensibilities these days.", "It's good to meet a fellow poet -- someone with an appreciation for *real text*. The others here, see, they don't really *get* it.", 'I get ya. When they really *click* it makes the world seem manageable. Good to be on the same page.', 'He gives you a thumbs up.', 'Yeah. I guess I owe you an apology for thinking otherwise. And again -- *great* shit.', 'He gives you a thumbs up.', "That's brutal, man. But, you know... Time will...", "That's... uhm...", "Yeah, yeah, I get that and it's cool. But...", 'Yeah...', "Yeah-yeah. I get it. These are *your* rhymes, they're from your life. Doesn't matter if they're robust, they're honest. So... thanks man.", 'Yeah...', 'He makes a half-hearted salute.', "Don't be a stranger.", 'He gives a salute with two fingers.', "Now it's turning into a... kind of a...", "Snow limbo, man. What's on your mind?", 'Make way for the master poet!', 'He greets you with a nod.', 'Still here, stuck in this damn jam, my man.', "What's up?", 'Hello again, my man.', "What's on your mind?", 'Welcome back!', "The days ain't going by any faster, believe me.", 'Feels like forever, like I was born on this here roundabout and this was all I ever knew. Just me and the metal and the tyres, the oil and the fumes of mazut...', "Yeah, imagine -- it's been a whole week already.", 'He snickers.', 'So, tell me... what do you need?', "Everyone's a critic, man.", "It's okay. I've been here a whole week already.", 'Back already?', 'He grins at you.', 'You sure are, my man.', 'He nods emphatically.', 'Hey there.', "It's the Jam, my man.", 'He motions toward the sprawl of lorries with a sweeping gesture.', "It's a traffic jam for the ages. Harbour gates up the street are shut tight. No explanation given. Workers on strike. Scabs agitatin'. An all-around clusterfuck.", "Meanwhile, we're all stuck here in long haul limbo for days upon days upon days...", 'Upon days.', 'Yeah, yeah -- exactly.', 'I am a gander and a hunter and a gatherer, feel like a traveller...', 'The man mutters to himself, accenting the beats as he goes.', "My man, you're alive!", 'Almost... kind of... sort of alive.', 'Man, what a day... I missed out on most of the action, but I heard it was quite the encounter.', 'Had a strong sense of *finality* to it.', "So what's next? You headin' back to Jamrock now? Talk is local Union muscle were behind it all, I'd reckon the case is closed... even if it kinda turned into a shitshow.", "Good luck with that, my man. Ain't easy being you, but hey, you're still breathin', right?", "I'm a bad guy now. There's things more important than holding a grudge. It's okay -- you've been through enough.", "We are what we are. And you're a cop.", 'Shoot.', "Sorry man, didn't mean it like that. Ask away.", "Hey, that's just what I heard. Old wives' tale. So -- what next?", 'Oh look...', "It's the cop who turned me into a bad person.", "I... uh... saw you poking around in lady driver's lorry. She in trouble?", "A little. She's okay. Troubled but -- a nice person. She left last week. Left me the keys to park her lorry if the jam should break.", 'Nothing, man. We just talked a bit -- about life and stuff...', 'So, is she in trouble or what?', "Oh man, that's like... a load off my mind. All that stress was messing up my rhymes.", 'Oh, you know...', "Tommy Le Homme's gonna be a musician. *Sprechgesang*, but with beats. I've got lot of free time on the road to hone my craft.", "Tommy L'Homme was taken.", "My real name is Jerry Lefitte -- Tommy's way better.", 'Yeah -- you too. Be safe, detective.', "It's that bad?", 'Man, what should I do... what should I do to help her?', 'Yeah, maybe I should just keep my head down... and work on my rhymes while I can.', 'Damn, I always warned her to watch herself... man, nothing to do now, I guess.', 'Maybe I should just keep my head down and work on my rhymes while I can.', "Nah, man, I was telling you the truth. I really didn't think it'd be her. She's okay. Sorta troubled but, still -- a nice person.", 'Nothing. We just talked a bit -- about life and stuff. She left me her keys, so I can park her lorry if the jam broke...', 'So, is she in trouble or what?', "Still better than me, I guess -- told you there's plenty of others who'd tell on her.", 'But... is she in trouble?', 'Hey, officer. Got a minute?']

Title: Disco Elysium
Dialogues: ['Agreed. The public relations potential of this is too valuable to let go.', 'The special consultant glances at his wrist-watch.', "I assure you -- I wouldn't consult for a corrupt unit.", "There's also a lot of outside help involved. Not only me.", 'Other losers too.', 'Shooting up churches never is. I was out of town, to be clear....', 'Yes.', 'I hear worries -- from systems analysts in Vesper and Messina. International risks departments in banks. People like that.', "Enrol him a year earlier and say he's fourteen. *If* he...", "It's tough. One of the toughest addictions to overcome. Comparable *only* to heavy synthetic opiates. Even morphine is easier to kick than alcohol -- statistically. The odds are against him. Especially at his age.", 'He slowly nods.', '...', 'Necessity-driven architectural design at its finest.', "Don't worry, Mikael, you'll learn all about it.", 'Fifty years ago this place was the heart of innovation.', "Feld versus Tricentennial -- I wish we could've witnessed that, Mikael.", 'On the outside – ruins. But what are ruins, Mikael? Detritus of lost epochs.', 'We are living in *very* interesting times, Mikael.', 'Remind me to give you that collection of essays on modern architecture, Mikael.', 'The significance of all *this* is hard to overestimate.', "I don't know what I'm even doing here.", "Hello! Isn't this a fine morning?", 'He nods to you, smiling.', '*memorable instance* when I had a chance to meet the head of Dominion Police of Königstein.', 'And, as you know, they have this very distinctive dress uniform with scarlet breeches and little cylindrical fur caps, I think these are called...', 'You daze off, as Trant tells you about the peculiarities of mounted police forces in central Occident.', 'How to climb that ladder, you say?', "I do know that the Lomanthangs used *sticks* to climb battlements, there's even a special technique for that.", "I'm just speculating *theoretically* here... Of course, there's also the method ancient Iilmaraans used to get into the huts of their enemies.", "If I'm not mistaken then it involved months of following a very rigid exercise regimen. No, *years*...", "In this case I suggest looking into the Seolite *invisibles* class. The word refers to their remarkable ability to traverse any environment in the most efficient way possible. There's this excellent investigative piece of journalism by...", 'Yes, I have!', 'There was this one time where I...', 'Actually no, I should not forget it, I should look into it myself, there are some really interesting techniques...', 'He stops, as Trant Heidelstam junior jerks his coat hem with an excited, almost silly look on his face.', 'physics, remember? But anyway...', 'Okay. I have some materials at home I could share with you...', 'Great. Great to hear that.', 'From an evolutionary point of view you could see this building as a logical conclusion to the more traditional *hut*.', "Then there's also the method of climbing that the ancient Iilmaraans used to get into the huts of their enemies.", "Alternative? I don't even have a *mainstream* way in, I'm afraid, although...", 'He points over the guardrail, to the sewage run-off there.', "There's a sewage pipe there, maybe that does something? Sorry I can't help more.", "No, I'm afraid I can't help you with this one, officer. It's just a regular day off for me and Mikael here.", "He pats his son's head.", "No, I'm sorry. As I said -- this is just a day off. We just arrived anyway.", "Sure, what's on your mind?", 'Yes, they even built a pleasure wheel, but that got destroyed in the war.', 'Yes. To lure in their star engineers. This part of Martinaise was nothing but reeds before Feld arrived. They had to make the prospect of living here *attractive*. It was supposed to become a global centre for innovation in cybernetics -- but history had other plans.', "Oh, I'm afraid it didn't end well for the boys.", 'But this story is a bit too *dark* for little Mikael here. Now if you were to ask about *tape computers*...', 'Officer!', "I told you this chapter of history wasn't on Mikael's curriculum yet. Let's keep this kid-friendly.", 'Tape computers.', 'He nods, wind tousling his suit jacket.', 'But also to write and send out press releases. The most notorious example being Le Décret de Mars.', "What's the March decree? I mean the radio transmission sent out to news agencies and world governments by the newly-created Commune of Revachol on the 7th of March in the year '02.", "It's a beautiful piece of text, actually. A singer-songwriter I know -- Charette -- called it a love poem to Revachol on her political concept album 'Bons baisers d'Insulinde'. You should read it. Every local library in Revachol stocks a copy of the decree.", 'I tried to get Mikael to memorise it.', '*Tried to*. Someone was much too interested in würms to be paying any attention.', 'Actually, no one knows. No one even knows what a computer made entirely of tape would look like! But word has it they were *very elegant* -- exquisite, alien-looking turn-of-the-century hardware...', 'He raises his finger, remembering something.', 'Ten years ago, I did a little... freelancing, I guess you could say. I was a special consultant for an exhibition at the Wompty-Dompty-Dom Centre in Vredefort, Oranje. It raised the same questions, and we had lengthy discussions with Paul Ockermann, who was head curator at the time -- this was before the twins Keith and Guy Joost joined the team -- trying to...', 'The Wompty-Dompty-Dom Centre for Contemporary Arts.', "The exhibition itself drew on Lagerman's notion of memory and so there were some parallels, that's why the head curator Paul Ockermann chose to...", "is a place you can visit if you're ever in Vredefort, and are ever in the market for an exhibition space slash contemporary art research centre.", 'But perhaps I should return to the tape computers. As I was saying, the device itself was very elegant, fragile even. One could write directly on the tape using a special chemical solution. The machine would then analyse the handwriting, perform operations and project output onto a white screen. It was a beautiful, delicate thing.', "Though I understand the socio-economic causes of the Revolution, it pains me to imagine the revolutionaries setting fire to this precious device. But so they did. The Feld Playback Experiment vanished into the fires of '07.", 'Yes, the official name of the prototype. Some sources report it as the Feld Playback *Experience*, but those are incorrect.', "Who knows? Maybe it was an accident, or maybe they didn't want the technology to end up in the wrong hands. Either way -- they're all gone now, all three versions of the prototype. Nothing but debris and ashes remains inside that building.", 'He takes a step back; the boardwalk creaks mournfully in the wind.', "*I* certainly haven't.", "Though I understand the socio-economic causes of the Revolution, it pains me to imagine the revolutionaries setting fire to this precious device. But so they did. The Feld Playback Experiment vanished into the fires of '07.", "Though I understand the socio-economic causes of the Revolution, it pains me to imagine the revolutionaries setting fire to this precious device. But so they did. The Feld Playback Experiment vanished into the fires of '07.", 'Yes -- tape computers. *And* Feld Electrical.', 'But of course! What else?', "He smiles and ruffles his kid's head.", "A-ha, but it's not just *any* empty old building!", 'He raises his hand to his eyes to shield himself from the pattering rain. All four of you turn to admire the mural before you.', 'What not a lot of people know is -- this used to be the R&D department of *Feld Electrical*. And Feld, which now sells ink cartridges, mostly, was once a top dog in the turn-of-the-century cybernetics boom.', "Apologies, it's an acronym for research and development, they don't use it anymore.", 'He smiles brightly, laugh lines around his eyes.', "You're probably more familiar with *RTD*, research and *technological* development.", "That's not surprising. Only a vestigial ink cartridge and ferrotape manufacturer remains.", 'He adjusts his suit jacket.', 'They started out as a midway electronics outfit in Königstein two centuries ago. After an aggressive move to Revachol, Feld became a global player in the emerging personal electronics market of the pre-Revolutionary era.', 'Still, Tricentennial was beating them in business machines.', 'But Feld had an ace up their sleeve. Or, should I say, they were *developing* an ace up their sleeve?...', "I'm mixing my metaphors here.", 'It was here in Martinaise -- possibly in this very building -- that they developed prototypes for a...', '...*tape computer*.', 'Mhm. An elegant folding mechanism of rollers and ferrotape ribbons, portable enough to be a take-it-home solution, revolutionizing business machines, possibly even bringing them to the average consumer.', "Which is a feat of engineering even today's giants Rehm, ICN, and ZAMM haven't achieved yet.", 'He grins, admiring the sentence he just produced.', 'Indeed, what?', 'Unfortunately their moonshot project never made it to the market.', "Feld's move to Revachol backfired. The Revolutionary government liquefied their assets and expropriated those very advanced prototypes. Possibly from this very building... or one of the adjacent ruins.", 'All of this was built by Feld, even the boardwalk. Wild Pines built Martinaise proper as a resort for their middle management, Feld built this side of town for R&D.', 'It was here in Martinaise -- possibly in this very building -- that they developed prototypes for a...', "He stops mid-sentence, realizing you're not listening.", "A-ha, but it's not just *any* empty old building!", 'He raises his hand to his eyes to shield himself from the pattering rain. All three of you turn to admire the mural before you.', "A-ha, but it's not just *any* empty old building!", 'He raises his hand to his eyes to shield himself from the freezing snow. All three of you turn to admire the mural before you.', "Well, that certainly depends. You know, the popular image of the Coalition is of a monolithic politico-military entity, but in reality, it's comprised of many interconnected, yet semi-autonomous components...", 'For instance, the offices of INSURCOM are responsible for military affairs. These offices are located in the Bank of the World building, just a few kilometres from here...', 'He points west toward the skyscrapers across the bay.', "But then there's also the Provisional Commission, as well as the Institute for Revacholian Culture, with its architecturally significant headquarters in Le Jardin.", 'INSURCOM is responsible for all aspects of the military occupation of Revachol. During the Revolution, they coordinated the efforts of the Occidental and Graadian invasion, but these days their function is primarily logistical.', 'Oh, the Institute is a marvellous organisation, my *favourite* part of the Coalition by far. Their mandate is two-fold: To export notable works of Revacholian culture throughout the Moralintern, while also importing the most important cultural products of the wider world to citizens of Revachol...', "There's an exhibition on Vespertine proto-expressionism that I can't wait to take Mikael to. We're working our way through the major artistic movements of the last cenutry.", "Of course there is! The Coalition's economic affairs are handled by the Bank of the World -- Revachol Mission. They operate in concert with the Institute of Price Stabilité in Sur-la-Clef.", "Ah, that's simple! You're looking for the Comité de Responsabilité de Revachol. It's a sort of clearinghouse for Coalition affairs in Revachol...", 'If you will, picture the Coalition as a kind of wheel. The hub of this wheel is the Comité de Responsabilité, and out from that hub radiate a great many spokes, which connect to INSURCOM, the Institute for Revacholian Culture, the Provisional Commission, and so on...', "I have a longstanding interest in political systems. You see, it's my personal theory that political systems are a lot like personalities. In other words, how a state organises itself is in some way the public expression of its innermost character...", 'The man smiles at you for a long moment...', "Of course, officer, we've only recently met. It would require a more thorough conversation than we have time for to answer a question like that. It's fascinating to think about, though, isn't it?", "The man's smile turns into a frown.", "Well, now, *that* is rather complicated. You can write to the Committee directly, but I understand that there's quite the backlog. A month or more, according to friends of mine who just so happen to know about this sort of thing...", 'Of course, if you could somehow contact Coalition Warship Archer, you could reach the Committee directly. But, well, that obviously presents any number of logistical and technical challenges.', "Why, officer, it's that gigantic aerostatic right over there. Have you really never noticed it before?", "A look of profound concern comes across the man's face.", 'That is certainly how the Coalition intends for it to be seen! You know, I once read a very interesting paper from Messina on the psychology of air-based artillery...', "Apparently its presence stimulates the *exact* same part of the neural cortex that more primitive cultures associate with divine judgment. Isn't that fascinating?", "That's very interesting. Most people I've met say it reminds them of a giant metallic dragonfly, but of course there's no right way to respond to a massive airborne artillery platform...", "Ah, well, it is one of the most heavily armed aerostatics to ever fly. I've heard it said that the Archer is capable of engaging whole fleets of lesser vessels *from multiple sides* simultaneously. How about that?", 'I believe that is intentional. You see, the Coalition are very sensitive to how they are perceived by the people of Revachol, which is why they generally prefer for their warships to remain at a discreet distance from major population centres...', "Ah, well, that's a relief to here. It would really be *quite concerning* if you hadn't been aware of it until just now...", "Fascinating! You know, in one sense, that's exactly what the Coalition intends. You see, they would prefer that most people in Revachol *don't* think of themselves as living under a *military* occupation. That's why they generally prefer to keep their warships at a discreet distance from major population centres...", 'A very astute question! You see, in addition to its role as a military warship, the Archer is also responsible for coordinating all Coalition communications and surveillance operations in Revachol.', "Not just watching, it's *listening* as well. I don't know the particulars, of course, but I would expect a warship like the Archer to possess the most advanced surveillance equipment available outside of Seol.", 'Well, I suppose you could rent a private aerostatic and attempt to rendezvous with Archer directly, but I must caution against it. Warships like the Archer are usually authorised to fire on unidentified aerostatics on sight.', "That might be the trickiest question of all. From a technical standpoint, it shouldn't be all that difficult. You simply require a radio transmitter capable of broadcasting on Coalition frequencies...", "The problem is that those sorts of radio transmitters are *tightly* controlled by the Coalition. Even the RCM doesn't typically have access to them outside of special joint operations...", 'All that said, someone with a powerful radio and a certain level of technical skill might be able to circuit-bend their way onto the Coalition frequencies...', "It's only too bad the old Feld engineers are no longer available. This sort of thing would have been *right* in their wheelhouse.", "In any event, it's a fascinating technical challenge. I'll be *very* interested to see how you tackle it.", "I do have some money, yes, but that's not what's really important here.", "He brushes it off like it's not a thing at all.", "Oh, no, I don't have it *on me*, officer, I was talking in more... general terms.", "He looks uncomfortable, his left hand squeezing his son's shoulder.", "I'm just spending time with my kid here, showing him around the lesser-known parts of our home town... It wouldn't be *wise* to carry huge amounts of cash on such expeditions!", 'he looks up again, a playful hint shining in his eyes...', "I don't know if you're familiar with this, but the Vespertine Department of Justice has published a rather interesting paper on the criminal profiling in former socialist states. Have you read it?", "If not, then you definitely should -- if not for tips and tricks, then just for theoretical curiosity. Anyway, that's just a little something that sprang to mind.", 'You were saying?', 'I do some Lo Manthang stick fighting now and then.', "It's an anthropological heritage of the Lomanthang people, a martial art of sorts, but what not a lot of books mention is that it also carries a *cultural* significance among the Lomanthangs, as it used to be the best means of showing off to look for a bride, which...", '... interestingly enough, brings us to the socio-economic structure of the traditional rural tribes of the Lo Manthang isles, which...', 'He goes on to give you a detailed overview of their way of life, the amiable, slightly nervous smile not once leaving his face.', 'I am boring you with details again. You were saying?', 'No, thanks to *you* for having me and little Mikael here to pick your brain... A very interesting conversation indeed.', 'Good evening!', 'He nods to you, smiling.', 'Hello again!', 'He nods to you, smiling.', '... and, Mikael, notice the windows? Especially with how there are no windows on the south side? This was to deal with...', 'A blond man stands next to his son, pointing to the weather-worn ruins. He sees you approaching and smiles...', 'You must be Kim Kitsuragi, right? I was just telling my son about this building. Not a lot of people realize the historic significance here. Very rich in *hypertext*.', 'Jan Kaarp and the collection of cultural hyperlinks.', "Oh yes. So, Mikael, they had to deal with monitor glare, especially in the summer. Mikael, say hi to the officers.", "He rests his hand on the boy's shoulder. The child stays hidden behind the hem of his father's coat, clutching to his würm-themed colouring book.", "Mikael's a little tired today. We spent all night trying to run Orbis on his radiocomputer. Have you heard of it? It's a programming language used in Graad. Quite tricky, but he wanted to play this Graad-made adventure programme. We've been getting *really* into würms lately...", "But I assume you're not here for giant würms when there are so many real things to see. Just as I was telling Mikael before -- this is where the Coalition landed in '08. We could be standing on what is the most interesting landmark in Revachol West.", 'He points to the building again.', 'Of course, lieutenant.', 'Take your time. Mikael and I have plenty to keep us occupied!', 'With that, you both turn back to the blonde man.', 'Whatever it is, he gives you an encouraging smile.', 'You, officer! Come to investigate the historic subtext of West Martinaise? I was just telling my son about this building. Not many people appreciate the historic significance here. Didn't mean to imply otherwise.", 'Ah, yes, their famous motto!', 'A fine example of technological optimism, from...', "Teleportation, Mikael. It's... generally thought impossible.", "Oh my god! I can't believe it!", 'Officer, be careful! Officer!', 'There could have been cameras. This needs damage control.', "Hello, I'm Trant Heidelstam. I believe we've met on several occasions.", 'Uhm...', "I don't *quite* know what I'm doing here. I was asked to participate as an expert -- I think I need to manage your expectations a little. We share custody.', "I wouldn't... quite say that. But, yes, he is displaying aggression not atypical of late-stage alcoholism.", 'What indeed?', 'I was asked to share my take on some of the more *obscure* theories developed in Königstein in the Thirties. Like -- partial psychotraumatic amnesia, group personality theory...', 'Again...', 'I was asked to share my take on some of the more *fringe academic* theories developed in Königstein in the Thirties. For example -- partial psychotraumatic amnesia, group personality theory...', 'No. I was just interested in the Feld building and the Martinaise Beachhead. And Mikael wanted to see Martinaise. It was a coincidence.', 'No problem.', 'What *am* I?', 'I was asked to share my take on some of the more *fringe academic* theories developed in Königstein in the Thirties. Regarding partial psychotraumatic amnesia. Group personality theory...', "I'm technically just a civilian advisor.", "Well... He doesn't have visible tremors. He talks without slurring. He can drive a boat. He's standing, reasoning. All good signs. But -- complete retrograde amnesia, episodic *and* semantic...", "but also mine with him before, when Harry did not seem to know who I was... It's all very interesting.", 'what do *you* think happened to you? Neurologically? Psychologically? And -- why not -- *socioeconomically*?', "Not when you phrase it like that. But I don't think critical theory -- I know everyone thinks this is far-fetched, pink academia, but still -- I don't think it should be off the table here.", "No, not like that, I'm not talking Vredefort School here. But, Harry, I asked you -- what do *you* think happened?", "Interesting. So at first he dipped his toes into it. Prepared. That's where he would have gotten the idea -- yes. Practice. And then he used alcohol to 'get there', so to speak...", "Well -- here is my theory: What if this is an absolutely normal reaction to the world we're living in? What if this is *not* a significant anomaly at all, something to be explained, approached as a defect? Look at the sensory input here...", 'He gestures toward the scenery.', "Look at the ruins, the neon, listen to the radio, the multitudes. The people. Live here for forty years... As a police detective, he's like a magnetic reader on the world-tape -- to borrow a known metaphor. Harry's been pushed *flat against it*. Total input.", 'Hard-wired to the free market...', 'He just needed for it to end.', 'He is *not* a cretin. And he *is* able to do work -- if not in his previous leadership role, then as a line detective.', "It's an urban myth -- a police detective who employs highly experimental investigative techniques. But, fine -- theory aside, what happened?", "but also mine with him before, when Harry did not seem to know who I was... It's all very interesting.", "As displayed in our interactions with him here, and also his interactions with the locals, where he did not remember being a law official... Were there eggs in the nest?', "Actually, you know -- this would indicate it was a male. This is far from anything in my field, but I think such nests are called 'bowers'. As I said, I'm only guessing. *I* didn't see it.", 'It must be robust, if it can move a whole helmet with its limbs...', 'It must be robust if it can move a helmet with its limbs...', 'He trails off, lost in thought.', 'As in cloning itself? What makes you think so?', "Well -- then it wouldn't matter if it's male or female. The bower would just be rudimentary behaviour from before the parthenogenetic mutation.", 'Very interesting.', "Such organisms are extremely vulnerable to disease. A single strain of bacteria could wipe out the whole species. We're probably looking at conservation efforts here...", "Interesting... Then it is *especially* vulnerable to disease. A single strain of bacteria could wipe out the entire species. The bower would just be rudimentary behaviour from before the parthenogenetic mutation.", 'Interesting...', "Then it is *especially* vulnerable to disease. A single strain of bacteria could wipe out the entire species. We're probably talking conservation efforts here...", "Hmm, yes. That would be a kairomone -- a pheromone that's seemingly beneficial to the host. It usually stimulates the affected nervous system -- not a human's, of course, but perhaps a predator's?", "There are species of bees that, under the influence of kairomones, take wasp larvae to their hives. Ants do the same with aphids thinking they're...", "Do you think this is how it's stayed hidden?", "Like a cephalopod's? Phasmids, I think, only have nerves in their heads and abdomens, though... there is a correlation between invertebrate size and intelligence. Was it...?", "Of course. I'm getting ahead of myself. Stick insects have primitive nervous systems. Still -- this creature would have a lot of surface area to put neurons into...", 'He nods.', "At that size, this creature would have a lot of surface area to put neurons into. It's basic geometry.", 'Incredible...', "The PR value of this is exceptional. 'Cop Discovers New Species.' Maybe even: 'Discovers the Insulindian Phasmid.' No... This says: science, news, human interest.", "You know, it's a really good thing you have that photo.", 'Incredible...', "It's a toughie that you don't have a photo. This would look very, very flashy in the papers. None of it says *vigilante murderers* to me at all. Great PR.", "We can still work 'Cop Discovers New Species' in there. I just thought it was noteworthy.', "This man would be Lilian's son -- Lilianovich.", 'The custom was overturned after the revolutions failed, but not before making it to Revachol.', "You know, Harry -- if I may interrupt -- it would help if you had *evidence*. Arche-typical even, dating back to many ancient tribal societies.', "You're right about that...", "Well, that's not exactly *proof*. It's a theory. But -- it *is* interesting.", "That's not *proof*, it's a description. But -- befitting a stick insect. If it's camouflaged to look like the reeds then it would have to be pretty large.", 'I would prefer *not* to partake in anything Union-related.', 'For political neutrality.', 'For the sake of political neutrality I would like to *not* partake in anything Union-related.', 'We could order a search. I could get people from EPIS on the island, entomologists, doctors. There must be signs of it in the reeds -- if we found the Insulindian phasmid, well -- that would be absolutely *exceptional*. The PR value alone...', 'Did he just say... Insulindian phasmid?']

Title: Disco Elysium
Dialogues: ['The ageing alcoholic is still there, breathing... The air in the room is stale.', "A lump of flesh is sticking out from under the blanket. It seems to be twitching from time to time, like the paw of an animal who's having a bad dream.", "A groan rises from the man's throat, dry like a death rattle... He's trying to say something in his sleep.", 'The light from the window is weak, but it seems like he is. His wild, unwashed mane bears a familiar ginger tone. Even the hair on his chest is coppery.', "No response. A pair of half-open bug eyes is staring back at you from the dark, empty and frozen. It's clear that the person behind them is not awake.", "The lieutenant's right -- the man's unwashed hair bears a familiar ginger tone. Even the hair on his chest is coppery. The light from the window falls into his half-open eyes.", "A pair of half-open bug eyes is staring back at you from the dark, empty and frozen. It's clear that the person behind them is not awake.", 'Fuckn... k... f...pi...', 'Suddenly the man starts growling. Three words manage to escape his mouth, along with a strong stench of alcohol.', "The pile of blankets grunts. It's hard to say if there's anything left you could do.", 'The pile of blankets grunts miserably.', 'Silence... Only heat emanates from the sleeping body.', "His hand falls back on the bed, limp and defeated. A loud snore escapes his mouth... He's asleep again.", 'And then falls back again, limp and defeated by sleep. A loud snore escapes his mouth.', 'You see a 60-year-old fat red-headed man passed out from large amounts of alcohol. And god knows what else. The smell of shit rises from his mouth.', "You don't have to take him down. He's already down."]

Title: Disco Elysium
Dialogues: ['A man lies on the boardwalk, his limbs bent and neck turned at an unnatural angle. Right next to him is an empty bottle of spirits. In his cramped hand: a chewing gum wrapper.', "He's wearing mud-caked boots, beige trousers and an old brown leather jacket with a bright blue lining. There are traces of kebab sauce on his chest.", 'Only some sunflower seeds remain in his soaked pockets. You already took the library card.', 'You find some sunflower seeds and a rain-soaked library card, folded into two. His jacket feels sodden and heavy under your hand.', 'The man has fallen through a crack in the boardwalk and hit his head against the metal bench. Coagulated blood covers his black hair. One of his feet is still dangling through the hole.', 'His expression is dull like the sea behind him, drops of water shining on his moustache. His eyes, empty and wide, look frightening in their frozen gaze.', "There's some dried blood on the metal bench, right where the corpse's head rests. The floorboards are rotten and slippery wet around the hole. An empty bottle lies nearby. A chewing gum wrapper is clutched in his fist.", "A dried chunk of blood covers the hair at the back of his head -- an open wound. It's sticky and cold to your touch.", "They screech under your feet, ominously. It's hard to say whether the dead man's weight was what caused the boardwalk to break... It definitely looks fragile.", "A 0.75 litre 'Touloula' vodka with its cap missing. There's hardly anything left inside.", "'Rubowski' spearmint chewing gum. Green leaves on the cover. The man's mouth is half-agape from the terror of the fall...", 'The blackness of death. Stench. You think you see white chewing gum too.', 'Careful. The wind blows hard, from the east.', 'The entire boardwalk creaks in the wind as you take a step back.', 'First you need to talk with the lieutenant, then report back to the station. This is too complicated to handle on your own.', 'A man lies on the boardwalk, his limbs bent and neck turned at an unnatural angle. Right next to him is an empty bottle of spirits. In his cramped hand: a chewing gum wrapper.']

Title: Disco Elysium
Dialogues: ["Our tenant, the policeman. I hope the waves don't keep you up at night. What can I help you with?", 'I told you before! No, there has been no listening to the radio. Not last week, not in the weeks before.', 'Anything else, now?', 'The old woman frowns. Her wrinkles frown with her.', 'Anything else?', 'A cold breeze rushes by. The old woman smiles.', "A radio? Hah -- no, we play no radio here. There is one in the shack, but it's never used.", 'These ears know every sound that belongs to this coast. I would know if I heard anything different.', 'Was that the nonsense they were spouting? Pah!', 'She shakes her head.', "No, I have no idea where they heard it. They've been in earshot all week, and no radio.", 'she says, shrugging.', 'Is there anything else I can help you with?', "Aye, even *I* can see that. I told you not to bring your trouble with you, policeman. We've got troubles of our own here...", 'Though I suppose you took the worst of it. Turns out you were your *own* ill omen.', 'The woman chuckles to herself.', "What do you expect? Police officers get put into dangerous situations all the time. Sometimes they get shot. It's a rough trade you're in.", "Still, I'm sorry to hear about your partner. He seemed to be a decent enough sort.", "What kind of foolishness is that? A cop's got to have a partner. That's in your nature, however you may deny it.", "But we've all lost someone we're close to, some more than once.", "That the best you can say about your *partner*? Sounds like it wasn't working out.", 'I warned you men with guns would be coming after you. They always are with your kind...', "So be careful. And don't be a hero.", "Wouldn't *dance* with you? Is that what you look for in a partner?", "What do you expect? Police officers get put into dangerous situations all the time. Sometimes they get shot. It's a rough trade you're in.", "I'm not sure those were the last of the men with guns, either.", 'There are always more coming for your kind, officer.', 'she murmurs softly.', 'Gone and hid things in there...', "She's usually a good tenant. And not a *stupid* one either.", '“Yes, I let my room to that Ruby girl…” She speaks slowly, wringing out a rag, after a long silence. Her hands move into the water bucket. Some water sloshes over the edge.', "As I've done before when she's been in trouble, or just looking for solitude. I've made it clear -- we welcome all kinds of people here.", 'She came last Friday. Left on Monday, in a hurry...', 'What has she gotten herself into, that girl?', "Yes, early, with the dogs -- around 8 o'clock, I think.", 'I cleaned it, like I always do.', 'No.', "She's good company. Knows how to talk to an old woman.", "At my age, you don't get a lot of quality conversation, so I really appreciate that about her.", 'No, she was mostly silent this time. Kept to herself...', "She tried not to let it show, but I could tell she hadn't come to fish -- usually she likes to cast a few lines, but this time she mostly stayed in her room.", "How would I know? She's a gruff one, but not violent. She doesn't go around toting a gun.", 'She looks back toward her shack, thinking.', 'Aye? Do tell.', 'A seagull flies overhead -- obviously a bad omen.', 'Exit from what?', 'No...', "She's a fighter.", 'That bad, is it?', 'Nothing of the sort.', 'Sure, she was no stranger to the bottle... she fit in, that way. But I only knew her to have a beer on the beach while watching the sunset...', "She isn't what you'd call a *drunk*. Even offered me some, from time to time. Said it was part of the camionneur life. But I never saw her lose control of herself, the way some people do.", "Not that I know of, though she was into nice music. She once showed me a few mixtape-milieus she'd made.", 'She brushes her forehead with the back of her hand. Water drips to the ground.', 'Although I guess she was pretty handy with the mechanical and technical stuff. Even fixed the heater in the shack. And maybe even then, because that's the kind of fishing village we've built.", "No, you're not. I've seen you around here before. Twelve years ago.
